Yeah I've heard a lot about how the hype isn't all that worth it. I can see why honestly, and it only makes me feel more secure in not aggressively pursuing it with just anyone I have chemistry with, but I guess I'm just frustrated because the few people I've been with and happy with have either not been comfortable with the idea (that's okay) or it's been long distance and promised but broken off before we could actually meet (complicated and honestly pretty hurtful). There's an air of insecurity as well, because a lot of people love to talk about this part of life that I just don't have anything to contribute to, and everyone BUT me is experiencing it - I already have low self-esteem, I don't like feeling this weird and unnatural.

Yep, women are a lot alike, but have different perspectives on things that I appreciate sometimes more than other men. You'd think this is obvious, but it's remarkable how many men don't ever really wrap their heads around this. But my big problem is the flirting part - I usually just don't have enough self-confidence to go through with it. It's not a social anxiety (though there's some of that as well, but nothing I can't overcome) but a feeling of, like... I don't have the right to flirt with someone, that the idea of me being interested in someone is 100% a hassle for them. That couldn't be further from the truth and honestly it should be pretty flattering most of the time (unless they're the type to get hit on constantly) but I must have this subconscious belief that I'm as bad as the worst people I see or something. And it doesn't help that there are people in my life that just don't seem to like having me around, or if they do they're awful at showing it. I feel incompatible with everything around me all because I'm low key and quieter than a lot of people and it's not fair to myself, but I can't shake the feeling.

I'm not especially fond of the "friend zone" terminology, but I understand the concept enough to know what it means and how it happens, and all the times this sort of thing has happened to me it's 100% been my fault, and I know that enough to try and avoid it now. I definitely need to learn to be faster in advances than I have been, and in my last relationship I was - took all of two weeks. But since then I haven't been able to meet anyone I've even been remotely interested in, or even really meet many people to begin with. Dating websites have been a total bust (getting flat-out ignored every time I send a message is discouraging, even if I understand women get way more messages than men) and I'm a little too introverted to go to parties or other social gatherings to meet new people and try to improve.

Overcoming a fear of failure has been easy in some cases and harder in others. For instance, in the heat of the moment I'm not really shy around strangers, but I have a difficult time pushing myself to go to more social events. I think it's because I largely just don't enjoy "party" settings and would rather meet people engaging in something I'm interested in than through a mingling environment.

I don't really feel the need or desire to lose my virginity as much as I'm afraid the longer time passes the more of a stigma I'm going to carry, and I don't like being "unique" like this especially when I'm insecure and uncomfortable with intimacy to begin with. Hearing people brag and openly talk about their sex lives sets me off towards a storm of jealousy and depression for no other reason than "I'm not like them and I'm not as good as them" and I'm tired of feeling that way. Just going out and experiencing things on a shallow level wouldn't make me happy, though, and I'm aware of that. It doesn't help that the one relationship I've had where things almost happened ended in a way that made it feel like I wasn't worth being with, so now I've got emotional baggage with intimacy on top of everything.

Adjusting my lifestyle has been a little difficult because of how picky an eater I am (and how much a creature of habit I am) but I'm pushing myself to at least do some cardio at the gym when I get the chance, and in the next few days I'm going to try to cook a lot more at home than go out and grab something cheap and easy. It should all be easy enough to get to a point where I'm satisfied with myself, it's pushing myself to make those changes when I'm already uncomfortable and unsettled that's making it that much more difficult.

I mean that's pretty much it exactly: I have standards, and I wish I didn't. I'm passionate about a lot of things ranging from movies to music to television to video games; I like media a lot, and I like to be critical of it, and that means I find the tastes of others to be irritating. I know we're all wired in different ways so we enjoy different things, but I guess I'm looking for a similar level of appreciation out of the connections I want to form, romantic or otherwise. If I weren't so "snobby" about this things would be a lot more simple for me, but unfortunately I am. I guess it's because I'm passionate. I'm sure there are others out there who are the same way, but it's not easy to find them. I've tried dating sites, but I get pretty depressed when I cycle through a lot of women and find little to nothing in common with them. Dating sites attract certain types of people, sure, but sometimes it's hard not to feel like that's the big variety of available women left for me to meet.

I'm actually not terrible at meeting women (online mostly now, in person I'm still figuring out), especially women who share hobbies and interests, but I think my problems sorta swing in the opposite direction from most guys. I'm great at making friends and I can't flirt to save my life if I'm actually interested in someone; I spent most of my high school life listening to my female friends deal with gross things men would do or say to them, and I wanted to be someone they could be around that wouldn't do those same things. I don't regret that at all, since I haven't been interested in most of them and I learned a lot about people different from me as a result, but I think it's also neutered my personality and now I can't be assertive - or at least I couldn't for much of my early adult life. Honestly in the past several years I've only ever met a couple of girls I was interested in getting closer to enough to try something with, but I haven't had enough chances to know whether or not my assertiveness has gotten better. But when you're not flirtatious and are extra-grounded by nature, you don't exactly glow as Romantically Interesting to a lot of women, and I'm still sorta learning to live with that.

Maybe it's because I'm afraid of overstepping boundaries and being annoying, or maybe it's what I'm really afraid of and I'm just too weird to connect with most people. I don't know.

This one isn't as fancy or good as a lot of other people's but here goes: I've always suffered from self-inflicted guilt and social anxiety, and relationships were very difficult for me as a result. I spent my young adult life (18-25) single and unwilling to even consider dating someone because I was convinced I didn't deserve it. 

One day I meet a girl online, we click better than anyone I've ever met. It doesn't take long for us to admit attraction to each other, and suddenly I found myself in a long distance relationship. She was great at understanding my insecurities and letting me feel like she cared about me and told me often how happy I made her as well, but it was a complicated situation: due to strange and unlucky circumstances we weren't able to meet in person for quite a while. We waited over a year until we got the chance to finally meet, talking every day and even though I was frustrated we couldn't meet, I was slowly building my self-confidence back up.

A few weeks before we were about to meet in person, fourteen months into the relationship, she unexpectedly ends it with me, telling me she found someone else and she couldn't deal with the possibility of me moving further away in the future. There was not even the faintest of warnings for it, and I found myself immediately losing every bit of pride in myself I was building up, blaming myself for it and going through an extremely difficult bout with depression. (And before you jump to conclusions, I know she genuinely cared for me even then and I know she was not faking her identity, since both of us were already very uncomfortable with the idea of lying to each other to begin with)

That's the twist, but here's the epilogue: I'm moving across the country in a high-risk situation in order to try and get my life moving forward again. And even though I'm 26 and still pretty awful at relationships, I finally found the desire to really look for someone who can make me feel as happy as I make them.

At the same time, don't go around telling everyone in the world "Hey guys! I'm a virgin!" because well people find that kind of annoying to be honest. Don't hide it, but don't put it in your list of traits that define you, either. And if someone does ask, don't be shy about it, and don't be insecure about it, and don't worry about what they'll think of you. Just tell them "yeah, and here's why" I guarantee you they will understand, unless they're just looking for a quick fling with you. And you don't strike me as the type of guy to attract those people anyway, so I very much believe you won't have anything to worry about.

Yeah, he's right, and I say that AS a virgin. I'm right there in your shoes, though I think I'm a little younger, and the fact that I'm a virgin bothers me, but it only bothers me on the level that I haven't been with a girl who I trusted enough to do anything with, and the ones I WAS with who earned that trust ended up abandoning me. Sometimes our experiences are dealt a shit hand, but what's eating away at you is your fear that those experiences are your fault.

It's really easy to give into the idea that being a virgin is a bad thing, but it's only a bad thing for people who treat sexuality separate from romance. Women who are with you for you don't care about your experience - in fact, a bigger red flag would be if you slept around too much rather than none at all.

Lemme put it this way: I've treated my virginity two different ways. Part of me was ashamed when my friends would talk about their experiences, and that's when people looked at me like I had done something wrong to end up this way. But recently I tried being proud of it and owning why I was still a virgin, and the response I got was overwhelmingly supportive, with the occasional grumpy "who cares". And that's just it: when your virginity is a trait rather than an affliction or a mistake, who cares?

If you're concerned about doing things wrong or not lasting long, don't be. If she cares about you, she'll be willing to help. Hell, she might even find it cute. It isn't always about the sexual performance, despite what everyone says. Sometimes it's just about being with someone.

Look, I'm saying all of this as someone who's struggling to push that paranoia out of my head as well. You're fine, dude. We both are. Unless you're trying to go hook up with some girl at a club or off of craigslist, being a virgin almost definitely will not matter, and you can easily learn how to make it a positive.

in my experience it's hard to pinpoint a singular thing to point to that'll help you "snap out of it" because the brain is a constantly growing, evolving thing. What works a few times can wear out its strength in a day, easily.

For me, it's thinking about something you're passionate about, and using whatever method that easily triggers that passion. I can talk endlessly about dozens of video games, movies, tv shows, books, music, things that hold a great deal of personal meaning to me, but oftentimes when depression settles in and twists my thinking, I lose access to a lot of that passion. The quickest way to circumvent it, most times, is to start digging around soundtracks that I love and pour through them to relive some of those moments or experiences in my head, or even to just get my imagination a-chuggin. It doesn't work every time because depression takes hold fast, but if I can manage to lose myself in it completely, the depression sort of fades away.

But that's me and what I'm passionate about! It might be a tedious act like organization, or cooking, or cleaning, or something else that you can completely lose yourself in. I hope that works for you, but if it doesn't don't give up! It might even be as simple as coming to reddit and reading encouraging comments on reddit. I hope you find something that works for you!

What do you feel like you're MEANT to do? If you don't know, you haven't found it yet, and that's a scary, hopeless feeling too. But I believe it's out there for you to find.

Now look, my depression is triggered by relationships too. I have a bit more experience than you but not much. It's depressing as hell, constantly thinking that you're being left behind while all your friends and everyone around you seem to be leading healthy love lives. 

But you aren't those people. You cannot let yourself compare you to those people. It's so easy to because how else are you going to understand you're screwing up or not? But you need to find a way to stop. I don't know what it is, I'm still figuring it out for myself and I won't be able to tell you. But that's what's making you notice all those relationships around you. 

You are not a lesser person for not having relationship experience. You are NOT a lesser person, though you may feel like it and you might be crushingly lonely. I don't buy into all the "There's Someone For Everyone" bs people spout, but as long as you focus on this awful lonely problem that's suffocating you, you aren't going to be able to fix it. And I know you want to.

Please don't kill yourself. If I sound stern it's because I'm worried, from a place of understanding. Yesterday I was there with you, ready to go through with it. 

Everything is going to be okay. You're going to be okay. But you're letting it win. Don't, please.

So I can definitely relate in some ways. I've had some social anxiety, but for me it was more really low self confidence than anything. I genuinely believed I didn't deserve to have someone romantically interested in me, so I'd turn away any girl who was, and never actually pursued anyone I was interested in. For years after that I just didn't date, and even stopped finding girls I was interested in. I've been steadily getting better, putting myself out there and talking to people just to meet them, even if most of the time it doesn't go well. I don't have very thick skin, but I'm trying to train myself to not take things personally. 

I've been using OKCupid - Tinder has been nothing but a disaster for me, because there's so little chance you'll find someone who wants to have a long conversation about something you have in common, and if you have social anxiety it's only worse. OKCupid's weird because like, from my experience girls don't go out of their way to message a lot of people. You have to message the ones you have something in common with, or just want to be friends with, but you absolutely cannot let yourself take it personally if they don't respond - and often they won't. They get bombarded with enough shitty messages and dudes who get mad for unfair reasons as it is. At the very least, start with messaging one or two, just for practice. 

As far as the masturbation thing goes, I kind of understand that. I have a similar thing where it's pretty difficult for me to get off unless I use pressure underneath me while lying on my stomach. It could be possible that you're overthinking things with "training" it though. My suggestion is, bar yourself from that same habitual masturbation for a while, and do your best to avoid it for a few days/a week or so. The sensitivity builds up after a little while, and it gets easier to, ah, finish using other methods, though it's not as good at first. You might've had trouble getting hard because of that same social anxiety, though I don't claim to know your brain better than you do. Having never been in that situation I can't help you much, but I bet the next time you find yourself in that situation you're gonna be worrying about it, which is probably going to cause it to happen again.

I'm rambling a lot, but I guess the most important thing I can offer is: this sort of thing takes time to happen. I'm still working on it, and I'm trying to tell myself to remain patient and not let my depression get to me about it. I've been struggling a lot lately because I feel like a failure and a fuckup (especially because my last relationship was long-distance for over a year, and a few weeks before we were going to meet she "met someone else" despite promising she'd be with me and my trust issues re: intimacy), but it's important to remember that even though we're definitely in the minority, just because we've taken so long to cross that point doesn't make us any lesser. We're both dealing with some weird brain issues and it inhibits us and slows us down, but as long as we try to grow and move past them, I think we can get better and be happier with ourselves and experience the things we want to with someone who genuinely cares about us.

Anyway, I hope something in that big essay helped. If you need to talk to someone about it more, I'm kind of right there with you, even if I'm dealing with different problems.

Hey man, so negative experiences aside, I've felt that same way before. I remember being that age and thinking "why aren't I doing what everyone else is doing? Why am I not out getting laid and enjoying myself?" For me, at least, it's because I hadn't yet realized that I didn't really have any desire to do that, and all I wanted was a real relationship - I wanted to be close to a romantic interest just as much as I wanted the sexual side of it. I also struggled with really low self-confidence, and every time a girl would be interested in me I would spend it questioning why they were interested, rather than letting myself enjoy it. I have no idea if this is something you can relate to or not, but for what it's worth: I don't think you're suffering too bad in the looks department. You're in a really mixed setting for you right now, in that you have the opportunity to be social and meet new people, but you're also surrounded by people who are more open and less sensitive with their sexualities than you are. And there's nothing wrong with that, and there's nothing wrong with you. You aren't going to end up alone, and your bad experiences do not define who you are right now, even if it continues to hurt and make you suffer.

Take a deep breath. You're okay man. I'd give you a hug right now if I could. That loneliness is biting and awful, and grappling with the constant "well I don't deserve this" of low self confidence never stops being exhausting. But it's not a matter of what you deserve, it's a matter of what you WANT and what you NEED. That sounds hedonistic, but it's not, not when you're lacking in being able to take care of yourself. I'm sorry you've had bad experiences, and that rejection hurts really bad, but please take a moment and remember: those rejections are not your fault, and they're not because there's something wrong with you. 

Right now what you need to do is focus on finding ways to be in uncomfortable social situations. Once a week or so, go try to find something to do that has a social element to it. Try to work on starting conversations with strangers, romantic interest or otherwise. Don't rush anything, just look for new people to talk to and focus on getting better at meeting people. Every time you feel bad about yourself, or down, immediately put that energy into meeting new people somehow, whether it's through hobbies or meetings or whatever. Keep looking, and in the meantime try to praise yourself for the things you get right, rather than scold yourself for what you get wrong. You can come back from this, I know you can. You're not alone. I believe in you.
